name: onboarder
description: Interactive architecture map of your workspace: endpoints → services → repositories → tables, cross-project links, AI summaries, chat, and Jira/ADO ticket → fix suggestions. Ships a bundled engine that analyzes the open folder in place — no upload, no Python, no server to run.

enumDescriptions: Download and run the bundled analysis engine locally — analyzes the open folder in place, no upload, no Python (recommended).
Use the hosted backend — uploads the folder for analysis. No local engine.
Spawn the Python backend via uv from onboarder.backendPath (for backend development).
onboarder.engineMode.description: How Onboarder analyzes your workspace. Ignored when onboarder.backendUrl is set.

onboarder.enginePath.description: Path to a prebuilt Onboarder engine (the folder containing onboarder-engine/, or the executable itself). Empty downloads the matching build for your OS on first use.

onboarder.backendUrl.description: Explicit backend URL, overriding onboarder.engineMode. A loopback URL (http://127.0.0.1:8000) is treated as a local in-place backend; any other URL uploads the folder for analysis.

onboarder.backendPath.description: Folder containing the Onboarder backend (the directory with pyproject.toml). Defaults to the backend/ folder next to this extension.

onboarder.frontendDist.description: Folder containing the built frontend (frontend/dist). Defaults to the frontend/dist next to this extension.

onboarder.startCommand.description: Command used to start the backend (run with backendPath as cwd). ${port} is replaced with a free port.

onboarder.autoReanalyze.description: Re-analyze the affected project automatically when you save a file (the open map refreshes in place).

scripts.package: npm run compile && npm run bundle-frontend && npm run bundle-engine && npx --yes @vscode/vsce package --allow-missing-repository
